findings.title: A command killed by an external signal is reported as a spawn failure.

findings.body:
**The dev.cycle and dev.review importers drop the host's `onDeprecatedAlias` wiring.**

- `OpRegistryEntry.importer` (src/kernel/types.ts:1081-1101) takes a `wiring` argument. Its documentation says that an importer that builds a driver factory passes `onDeprecatedAlias` through. In `--json` mode, the CLI passes a silent sink.
- The dev.cycle importer at line 340 ignores `wiring`. It also does not pass `drivers` to `makeDevCycle`, so cycle.ts:435 calls `createDriverFactory()` with no config.
- dev.review at line 290 has the same problem.
- If a cq.json role uses provider `'ai-sdk'`, `stderrAliasNotice` writes to stderr during a `--json` run (src/driver/factory.ts:557,566). This breaks I1: "In machine mode (`--json`) stderr stays empty."

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix (dev.cycle; apply the same change to dev.review at line 290)</summary>

```diff
-    importer: () =>
+    importer: (wiring) =>
       Promise.all([
         import('./cycle.js'),
         import('./effects.js'),
         import('../../adapters/forge-github/ghEffects.js'),
         import('../dev/denylist.js'),
         import('node:fs/promises'),
+        import('../../driver/factory.js'),
       ]).then(
-        ([m, effects, ghEffects, denylist, fs]) =>
+        ([m, effects, ghEffects, denylist, fs, driverFactory]) =>
 ...
             return m.makeDevCycle({
               effects: dev,
+              drivers: driverFactory.createDriverFactory(
+                wiring?.onDeprecatedAlias === undefined
+                  ? {}
+                  : { onDeprecatedAlias: wiring.onDeprecatedAlias },
+              ),
               gh: ghEffects.makeSubprocessPrEffects(input.repoRoot),
```
</details>

As per coding guidelines: "In machine mode (`--json`) stderr stays empty".







Also applies to: 388-389
